title: Mixed-precision safety-net: calibration pipeline and regression harness for GPTQ/AWQ
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Objective: Build an automated calibration and regression harness that validates INT8 weight-only profiles produced by GPTQ/AWQ flows and exercises FP8 fallbacks and mixed-precision safety nets. This ticket covers orchestration, golden-answer regression, telemetry gating, and an automated canary pipeline for new calibration artifacts.

Background: Our weight-only INT8 profiles are increasingly used across model families. Several customers need strict SLA guarantees; regressions after calibration runs have caused small but customer-visible answer deltas. We need a reproducible gate that validates numerical fidelity against golden prompts, exercises an FP8 mixed-precision fallback path for edge cases, and integrates into CI/CD for model onboarding and profile updates.

Scope:
- Orchestrate calibration artifacts from GPTQ and AWQ toolchains into a standardized profile registry.
- Build a regression harness that runs golden-answer diffs across a curated prompt set for quality, latency, and token distribution metrics.
- Implement automatic checks for catastrophic drift, metric thresholds, and latency/cost regressions.
- Add a mixed-precision runtime verification that triggers an FP8 fallback simulation when INT8 profile confidence is low.
- Surface per-profile telemetry and a scoring signal used by canary gate and rollout policies.

Out of scope: retraining, new quantization algorithms, UI work in Console (Console follow-up ticket will add dashboards), and private deployment packaging (will be handled in a separate Private-vpc ticket).

Implementation notes:
- Use the existing profile registry proto (runtime-2.3) as the artifact contract. Profiles must include metadata: model-commit, calibration-seed, per-layer quant stats, confidence scores, and signer checksum.
- The harness will run three passes: smoke sanity (sanity inputs + logits consistency), golden regression (golden prompts + answer-diff scoring with thresholds), and stress verification (long-conversation drift + perf tail latency).
- For mixed-precision safety-net, add a deterministic FP8 emulation mode that runs on CPU/GPU depending on canary environment; this helps validate behavior without requiring production FP8-enabled hardware.
- Telemetry: emit per-run metrics to telemetry-level "quant-profile-validation.v1" with tags {profile_id, model, variant, run_type}. Metrics: answer_delta_pct, perplexity_relative, latency_p50/95/99, token_cost_estimate, fallback_triggered.

Acceptance criteria:
- New calibration profiles registered by GPTQ/AWQ flows automatically trigger the regression harness in CI.
- Harness produces a validation report and a pass/fail signal saved to the profile registry.
- Canary pipeline denies rollout on fail or on high 'answer_delta_pct' (>2.5% across golden set) unless manually overridden with documented justification.
- FP8 fallback simulation runs and records a deterministic fallback decision for any profile that triggers it.
- Telemetry and artifacts stored in S3 (s3://redwood-quant/profiles/validation/YYYY-MM-DD/) and linked in the profile registry entry.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Golden prompt set may bias toward specific languages or domains. Mitigation: include stratified prompt set across domains, lengths, languages; create a rotation schedule so golden set evolves monthly.
- Risk: False positives on acceptable semantic divergence. Mitigation: include both token-level delta and semantic similarity (embedding cosine) thresholds; run human-review for borderline failures and capture labels for training a fallback classifier.
- Risk: Canary slowdowns increase CI time. Mitigation: run full stress suite in nightly pipeline and a trimmed golden + smoke in PR-level canary.

Next steps:

2) Implement harness runner and integrate telemetry emission (first PR target: runtime-2.4 branch).
3) Wire the canary gating logic into the deployment orchestration (ops-runbook stub attached).
4) Add human-reviewflow for borderline regression failures (follow-up PM ticket).
